small_guidance:
- The GEMM dominates (1024×8192×8192 ≈ 137 GFLOPs); add larger autotune configs (BLOCK_M=128/BLOCK_N=256/BLOCK_K=64, BLOCK_M=256/BLOCK_N=128/BLOCK_K=32, num_warps=8, num_stages=4) and add a GROUP_M=8 swizzle on the program grid to improve L2 reuse across N tiles.
- Pre-transpose weight to (K, N) contiguous once in `__init__` so the inner B load is along the contiguous N axis (`tl.dot` prefers K-contig A and N-contig B); current `weight.stride(0)=K, stride(1)=1` forces strided B loads.
- The logsumexp epilogue currently materializes the full M×N clamped matrix and reads it twice. Fuse the row-reduction directly into the GEMM epilogue when BLOCK_N covers a meaningful slice — at minimum, make logsumexp single-pass online (track running max and rescale sum) to halve its bandwidth.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as a persistent split-K-free GEMM where each program handles one full output row tile (BLOCK_M rows × full N=8192) by streaming N in BLOCK_N chunks; accumulate per-row online logsumexp (running max + rescaled sum) inside the same kernel and never write the M×N intermediate. This eliminates ~270 MB of intermediate traffic and folds clamp+LSE+Mish into the GEMM epilogue.
- Alternatively, split the work as two kernels but skip materializing Y: a streaming GEMM that emits, per (row, N-tile), the partial (max, sum_exp) into small per-row scratch, then a tiny reduction kernel combines tiles into the final lse and applies Mish. This keeps tile sizes flexible while removing the M×N store/reload.
- Since K=8192 is large, consider split-K with atomic-add into a row-accumulator and pair it with a final epilogue kernel doing clamp+LSE+Mish; tune BLOCK_K up to 64-128 with num_stages=4 to overlap the long K-loop.
